author: Mmnin
quote:
It's an above average life/crime sim, nothing more. Perhaps revolutionary for interactive story production values, but this was marketed as the next great GTA mainline game and presents very little of the GTA formula everyone has expected and found so entertaining in the franchise. With tons of unnecessary restrictions, added surprise content that often is tedious or doesnt make sense, and extremely tame story, main characters and dialogue, this game is excessively mundane compared to its predecessors. 

The graphics, animations, and physics are all very lifelike and beautiful for what is there, however noticeable corners were cut for the sake of "ethics." Many of the things you think you should be able to do, you won't be able to. For every unneeded addition is one equally nonsensical omission, and even with all the ideas, attention to detail, and tech that went into its creation, it still often feels like just old game design with a pretty coat of paint, not something you would expect from a game 13 years in the making touted as the best game of all time. 

Performance issues. While I have only experienced a handful of mostly non intrusive glitches, the internet is currently overrun with examples of in-game performance issues affecting gameplay, again, not something you would expect from the budget and time spent on this development, not when other companies are putting out near flawless complete content at launch with a small fraction of the budget. Scope of game should not be an excuse to release unfinished or low quality content and it shouldnt excuse those issues from affecting the scores which indicate the overall game experience.

Now probably the biggest issue with GTA VI. 
With everything considered, this game has been overhyped industrywide for some reason unknown to consumers in its final form. The reviews that have given the game a perfect score while admitting the game has its flaws were not genuine in their scoring and I now question the legitimacy of all outlets. If this wasn't a GTA game, but labeled as a GTA spinoff or some other new property, marketed simpy as a life/crime interactive story experience from the makers of the Red Dead Redemption and GTA series, then I would say this game is deserving of 96/100, but with the marketing push, forcing a position as the coveted "greatest game of all time" and the premature GoTY push, and the fact that this simply is not the game fans had obviously expected, being a new flagship GTA, I have to use this review and platform to help counter the industry corruption in GTA VI's favor.

No this is not the greatest game of all time. It is an industry wide push to ensure that a particular type of game by a particular company is labeled such so that more people will be socially coerced into purchasing. GTA VI does nothing that other games in the life/crime sime genre haven't done before and in some cases even does it worse. It simply does a lot of it with a bit more polish and a higher budget. It is not a revolutionary title as claimed, no moreso than Read Dead Redemption 2 was. 

What pours more salt on this infected wound is that this game is digital only to minimize returns and prevent resells. They knew many players would not be happy with the gameplay changes, so they timed the launch to steal the "Greatest game of all time" label using arguably false review scores to propel and secure word-of-mouth/hype sales. This was the overall and defining "gimic" of this release, to pull the wool over the eyes of the consumer and heist as much money as possible at launch.

The saddest thing is, is that GTA VI does show a lot of developer love and labor. It does open the door to more "movie-esque" interactive high production experiences, albeit more interactive novel than game, and on its own it doesnt deserve the amount of controversy it is having, but we'll never know honestly how well this game could have performed on its own merits thanks to the commercial manipulation that has taken place.

game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Mmnin
quote: Fun gameplay and full game experience but lacks buildup. While Splatoon Raiders has addictive and enjoyable mechanics borrowed from its multiplayer sibling and uncludes a few surprisingly large scope boss experiences sprinkled throughout, midway the game begins to depend on recycled material enhanced only by increased chaos. This greatly limits the overall experience. The final encounter, though a unique design and grand in scope, sadly abandons the established mechanics almost entirely in favor of disconnected engagement. A fun experience for Splatoon's first primarily single player campaign and hoping future offerings advance beyond these creative limitations.
